timeline.change: Development begins; design work follows in 1998, and Lance Scott's ED² (France) proposal is picked in late 1999
Launched in Japan on 7 October; production began in September. Lexus starts US sales of the GX 470 twin in November
Australian launch with the new 4.0 L 1GR-FE V6 (179 kW), the 1KZ-TE diesel and the 2.7; 4-star ANCAP. 14,639 sold in Australia that year

Five-speed automatic arrives for the V6

Production ends; the J150 Prado replaces it in September

identify.intro: The Prado 120 looks a lot like a Lexus GX 470 and shares its platform with the 4Runner and FJ Cruiser. Read the model code and the engine bay, not the badges.

items.head: Model code = engine + body
items.body: GRJ = 1GR-FE 4.0 V6, KDJ = 1KD-FTV diesel, KZJ = 1KZ-TE diesel, VZJ = 5VZ-FE 3.4 V6, RZJ = 3RZ-FE and TRJ = 2TR-FE 2.7 fours. Toyota's own list shows 120/121 as five-door codes and 125 as the three-door.

items.head: Copper or aluminum injector seats
items.body: On a 1KD-FTV, trucks built from August 2007 have aluminum injector seats; earlier trucks have copper ones. Ask for receipts if the copper seats have been replaced.

items.head: Air or coils at the rear
items.body: Electronically controlled rear air suspension came on the Australian Grande and top Japanese grades (TZ G Selection). Look for the air springs and compressor before you price a lift.

items.head: Rear diff
items.body: ExplorOz owners say Australian GX/GXL trucks have a rear LSD, while VX and Grande have an open rear diff with traction control. Some markets list a rear diff lock, so check for the switch and confirm it works.

items.head: Prado or rebadged GX?
items.body: IH8MUD has threads on rebadging GX 470s as Prados. A 2UZ-FE V8 and a US VIN mean it's a Lexus GX 470, whatever the tailgate says.

paragraphs: Toyota never sold the Prado 120 in the United States. North America got the same truck as the [[lexus/gx470|Lexus GX 470]], with a V8. NHTSA allows vehicles at least 25 years old to be imported without meeting US safety standards, and counts the 25 years from the date of manufacture. Production began in September 2002 (Japanese sales on 7 October 2002), so the earliest J120s become eligible from September 2027. The last, built in August 2009, follow in 2034. EPA's separate exemption (Form 3520-1, code E) needs the vehicle to be at least 21 calendar years old and in original configuration, so from 2027 the NHTSA rule is the one that matters.

Canada is more relaxed. Transport Canada lets in vehicles from outside the US and Mexico once they're 15 years old by month and year of manufacture, so every J120 has qualified since August 2024. That doesn't help Americans: a Canadian-registered Prado 120 still has to reach 25 before it can be brought into the US. When the time comes, check your state's titling and emissions rules (California especially) before you buy.
